# Review checklist

Run it on every post file before you hand it over (Step 5) and after every revision. Fix what fails; never hand over a file that fails an item without saying which and why.

## The brief

- [ ] Every size and iteration in the brief has a frame, and nothing extra. Count: sizes x iterations = frames.
- [ ] File names follow `04-brief-intake.md` section 3; V1 and V2 differ in the testing variable and in whatever copy the brief gives per iteration, nothing else.
- [ ] Open items are listed in the file header and in the hand-off.

## Copy

- [ ] Client copy is verbatim in every frame: same words, case, punctuation and apostrophes. Read it against the brief, word by word, after the line breaks.
- [ ] Nothing added: no disclaimer, number, review, price, retailer or subhead the brief does not carry.
- [ ] Sizes without a `sub` slot drop the subhead; no other slot was dropped.
- [ ] No long dash (em or en dash) anywhere you wrote.
- [ ] Line breaks fall on meaning and match each layout's line count.
- [ ] Copy you wrote follows `01-brand.md`: purchase in the headline, proof in the subhead, no credit-score headline on every piece, no shame, no promises.

## Layout and images

- [ ] Every `data-use` is a code in `02-studio-kit.md`; every listed slot is filled.
- [ ] Banner jobs use one pattern across all sizes (P3A and P3B, or P4A and P4B, count as one pattern).
- [ ] Banner text uses the pattern's spans (P2 one span per bar, `t1` for the setup and `t2` for the punchline; P3 `t1`, `t2`, one `ta` per sentence; P4 one span per line).
- [ ] Every image is `library:`, `product:` or an `upload:` file the person confirmed they have.
- [ ] Photos: a person is the focal point and uplifted; brand fit is on-brand (or "with care" with a reason); the subject matches the message; each size has a crop that keeps the face clear of the copy.
- [ ] Products: believable relative scale (`data-scale`), categories mixed when the message is breadth.
- [ ] `data-size` used only after rebreaking, never under 70%. Frames where the copy is tight are named in the hand-off.

## Hand-off

- [ ] The file is complete (every frame), named for the job, and the note says what to do in the Studio.
- [ ] Organic posts carry caption, hashtags and alt text per slide.
- [ ] Stock photos used in paid media: "stock licence to confirm" noted.
